name: Good AI Practice in Manufacturing
blurb: The FDA and EMA principles applied to production.
title: Good AI Practice in Manufacturing
answer: The ten FDA and EMA principles of good AI practice explicitly include manufacturing. For plants this means risk based use, high quality data, documented models, and monitoring through the product lifecycle.

reading.body:
The FDA and EMA's ten principles of good AI practice apply directly to manufacturing, not only to drug development.

The principles are risk based use, high quality data, documented models, and monitoring through the product lifecycle. A plant that already runs a quality manual can fold them in, so AI projects inherit the same expectations as any other controlled process. That matters because manufacturing AI sits close to the product, where an undocumented model or drifting input is a batch problem rather than a software problem.

The data covers the principles and one instruction for adopting them. It does not name the ten principles individually, describe how regulators will inspect against them, or say what compliance costs. It also does not connect the principles to compute or power, and nothing here supports a claim about either.

explainer:
The FDA and EMA principles apply to manufacturing as much as to clinical work. In a plant they translate into concrete practices: decide where AI is justified by assessing risk, use representative and well governed data, document how models were built and tested, assess performance in the actual operating context, monitor through the lifecycle, and give operators clear information about what a system does and its limits.

Building these into the site quality manual and standard procedures means every new AI project inherits them by default rather than reinventing governance each time, and it gives inspectors a recognisable structure.
